findings.what: The accept item "loading a glyph preset in a dither context returns a warning and a pixel renderer" is not tested. The only glyph-in-dither test asserts the opposite: glyph_ramp is kept and warnings == [].
findings.why: An explicit acceptance criterion has no test. The one test that touches it exercises a different semantic: availability = whole registry, so any app keeps any registered renderer. Nothing proves the implemented fallback path matches the card.
findings.fix: Add a test that loads glyph_v3.json with app='dither' and available={'pixel'} (the dither host's own renderer set). Assert renderer.name == 'pixel' and exactly one warning that names 'glyph_ramp'. Keep the registry-default test, but state in its docstring that the app host must pass `available` to get the card's behaviour.

findings.what: In from_json, `preset = ...; return preset` is a needless temporary. The nested conditional for `context` is hard to read.
findings.fix: Return directly from each branch and compute `context` with an if/else.

findings.what: In _from_legacy, legacy files that carry v3 section keys (pipeline, effects, app, masks and so on) are silently dropped. They are excluded from `extra` via `_V3_TOP`.
findings.why: This contradicts the contract's preservation of unknown keys. The data loss is silent, although the test deliberately protects the typed sections from overwrite.
findings.fix: Either document the drop in the docstring or stash the colliding keys under a namespaced `extra` key.

regression: none (new module; PipelineSpec bridge is additive; no frozen behaviour touched)
renderer_invariants: all six hold (this card adds no renderer; the preset only reads the registry through list_renderers)
tests_that_cannot_fail: test_shipped_presets_are_discovered: the second assert (`_all_files()`) is implied by the first
notes: The dither-context accept item conflicts with the pass-2 decision to remove the per-app renderer table. The `available` parameter can satisfy both, but only if a test pins it, so the fix is test-only. If the human wants the default call from_json(glyph, app='dither') to warn with no `available`, an app-to-renderer table is needed again. That is a contract/card clarification, so escalate. No E8/E9 issue: the AST import test is real and no host access is present. Maths: none, since this card has no renderer or effect maths.
